title: Market Failure Adventure 1: Externalities
welcome_lead: Today you'll measure positive and negative externalities and meet Pigouvian taxes.
meta_desc: Economics: positive and negative externalities of production and consumption, Pigouvian taxes.
final_note: You distinguished four externality types and applied Pigouvian remedies.

concepts.def: Spillover cost or benefit on third party
Marginal private cost — borne by producer
Marginal social cost = MPC + ext cost
Tax equal to marginal external cost

walkthroughs.body_html:
Externalities arise when a third party feels costs or benefits.

Negative production: factory pollution (MSC > MPC).
Positive production: R&D spillovers (MSC < MPC).
Negative consumption: cigarettes, sugar (MSB < MPB).
Positive consumption: vaccination, education (MSB > MPB).

Market equilibrium ignores external costs/benefits.

For a negative externality, output Qe exceeds the social optimum Q*. The triangle between MSC and MPC over (Q*, Qe) is the deadweight welfare loss.

Symmetric logic for positive externalities and under-production.

Arthur Pigou (1920) proposed taxing producers by the marginal external cost — internalising the externality.

Subsidise positive externalities by marginal external benefit.

Practical issues: measuring the externality, regressive impact, evasion. Carbon taxes and tobacco duties are real-world Pigouvian taxes.
